specification.problem: Approximate synthesis of the single-qubit rotation exp(-i f(phi_1,...,phi_k) X) with a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) framework, using two primitives (product and reciprocal/nonlinear), with few ancillas (about 3 for multiplication and reciprocal). Inputs are rotation angles, not binary registers.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance: the product primitive for two small angles a,b, mapping to approximately exp(-i a b X) on one target qubit with up to 3 ancillas, read out by statevector on the success branch. Also give the ideal target formulas for the reciprocal primitive and the composition rules. The exact RUS gate sequences, failure corrections, and amplification are NOT in the abstract and remain outside scope. The paper's cost analysis of conventional reversible arithmetic is also out of scope.

equations.label: Target rotation
equations.description: Desired output single-qubit rotation on target t.
equations.abstract_quote: approximate synthesis of single–qubit rotations of the form $e^{-if(\phi_{1},\ldots,\phi_{k})X}$
equations.justification: The abstract states the target form directly.

equations.label: Product primitive ideal action
equations.description: The multiplication gadget on the success branch approximates a rotation by the product of the angles, with error of higher order in a,b.
equations.abstract_quote: RUS circuits for approximate multiplication and reciprocals
equations.justification: Multiplication of angles implies the effective angle ab. The sketch notes a commutator-like second-order structure, but the exact gate sequence is not in the abstract.

equations.label: Reciprocal primitive ideal action
equations.description: Candidate success-branch rotations for the reciprocal gadget. Both are smooth reciprocal-like functions; for |theta| >> c, arctan(c/theta) is approximately c/theta.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes these forms. The abstract only says reciprocals are obtained, and the exact function is a guess.
assumptions: Which form the paper uses is unknown

equations.label: Composition rules
equations.description: Addition is concatenation of commuting X-rotations. Multiplication and inversion use the two gadgets, with angles rescaled into the accurate region.
equations.abstract_quote: smooth computable functions $f$ can be synthesized from two basic primitives
equations.justification: X-rotations commute, so addition is exact. Nesting of the primitives follows from synthesizing smooth f from two primitives.
assumptions: Rescaling keeps all intermediate angles small

equations.label: RUS success branch and readout
equations.description: Post-selected on the ancillas giving 00..0, the target is rotated by exp(-i f X) from |0>, giving <Z> = cos(2f). The effective angle is f = arccos(<Z>)/2 for f in [0,pi/2].
equations.justification: For |0> under exp(-ifX), <Z> = cos^2 f - sin^2 f = cos 2f. This is standard single-qubit algebra.

registers.name: t
registers.role: target qubit carrying exp(-i f X)

registers.name: anc
registers.role: RUS ancillas, measured mid-circuit and reset for reuse

specification.initial_state: Target |0>. Ancillas |0>, or |+> where the sketch's entangler construction uses them (assumption).

steps.description: Initialize the target and ancillas. Choose small a,b so the second-order approximation is accurate.
Apply the product gadget: alternating rotations R_X(a), R_X(b) with CNOT/CZ entanglers (guessed from standard RUS constructions), then measure the ancillas.
If the outcome is all-zero, accept. Otherwise apply the known Pauli correction or restart, and reset the ancillas.
Optionally compose with the reciprocal gadget or concatenated X-rotations for general f.
Read the target statevector on the success branch and extract f from <Z>.

specification.measurement: Ancillas are measured in the Z basis, with all-zero as success. The target is read by statevector or tomography on the success branch. If counts are required, measure only the target Z bit, keeping Qiskit's little-endian order in mind.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Post-select on the ancilla all-zero outcome, estimate f = (1/2) arccos<Z>, and compare with the ideal f. The expected number of repeats is 1/p_s.
assumptions: Inputs are rotation angles given as gates, not binary registers
Chosen scope is a single product gadget instance
Success probability is bounded below by a constant for restricted angles
Failure branches are fixable by Pauli corrections or a clean restart
Gate sequences are guessed, not from the abstract
Approximation error is controlled by small-angle scaling
